description.en: A source-verified MiniMax H3 vlog prompt with attached video evidence from @bmx_ai13.
description.zh: 由原作者公开 X 帖提供并已核验视频结果的 MiniMax H3视频提示词。

prompt:
ULTRA REALISTIC 15 SECOND PERSONAL HOME VIDEO. 1080p render of 4:3 early 2000s MiniDV tape footage. Single continuous handheld take, no cuts. Dialogue driven, Hinglish. Title: THE FRINGE.

CONCEPT
She just got a fringe cut and immediately regrets it. Her friend films her checking herself in a shop mirror instead of reassuring her. The clip ends before she decides how she feels.

SUBJECT LOCK
Indian woman, early twenties, warm medium brown skin, realistic pores, faint under eye shadow, minimal makeup. Dark brown hair loosely tied back with a freshly cut blunt fringe sitting slightly too short and too straight on her forehead, loose cut hairs still on her shoulders. Oversized cream knit sweater with stretched cuffs, blue jeans, white sneakers scuffed at the toe, small canvas shoulder bag across the body. Same face, hair and outfit for the full 15 seconds. Fidgeting, pushing the fringe left then right.

SECOND VOICE LOCK
The friend holding the camcorder is never seen, not a hand, not a shadow. Voice only, young female, close to the mic, deadpan. Never addresses an audience.

SETTING
Narrow front room of a small neighbourhood salon, late afternoon. Wall mirror with a chipped frame, a swivel chair, combs in a jar, a plastic cape draped over the chair back, a pedestal fan turning, sunlight coming in flat through an open doorway. Lived in and unstyled. No visible brands, no logos, no readable signage.

CAMERA
Raw handheld MiniDV camcorder held at chest height from behind and to the side, so most of her face is seen only in the mirror reflection. Autofocus hunting between her actual head and the reflection, never settling. Exposure pumping between the bright doorway and the dim interior. One unmotivated zoom into the mirror that goes soft. Framing crooked, her head near the top edge. Tape noise, interlace combing, one dropout glitch. No stabilization, no gimbal.

BEATS
0:00 to 0:04 She leans into the mirror, lifts the fringe with two fingers and drops it, already unhappy.
0:04 to 0:09 The exchange, quick, overlapping, both half laughing.
0:09 to 0:12 Dead air. She stops touching it and just looks at herself. Nobody speaks for three full seconds, only the fan.
0:12 to 0:15 She turns to face the camera for the first time, says the last line, does not wait for an answer, tape cuts.

DIALOGUE
Hinglish code switching, natural overlapping delivery, flat and unprojected.
0:04 She says Sach batao, kaisa lag raha hai
0:06 Friend off camera says Sach sach?
0:07 She says Ruko, mat batao
0:12 She says Grow to ho hi jayega na
Visible mouth movement with bilabial closure on m, b and p. Friend lines off camera only, closer to the mic.

AUDIO
Diegetic only. Pedestal fan oscillating, scissors clinking into a tray, a scooter passing the open door, a chair squeak, her sleeve brushing the mirror, faint hand noise on the camcorder. No music, no score, no added ambience beds.

STYLE RULES
Nothing dramatic happens. No posing, no makeover reveal energy, no hero framing, no beauty lighting. Realism comes from the awkward laugh and the dead air. If she performs for the lens the illusion breaks.

NEGATIVE
No music. No subtitles. No captions. No watermark. No timestamp. No slow motion. No color grading. No lens flare. No shallow depth of field. No visible second person. No brand logos. No readable text.

LAST FRAME
Her half turned toward the lens, fringe uneven, frame crooked and slightly underexposed, one frame of tape tear, hard cut to black. Absolutely no on screen text, no title card, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no signage of any kind in the final frame.
